subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Antimetabolites in clinical oncology: folate antagonists, pyrimidine analogues and toxicity rescue

steps.tx: Folate analogues block single-carbon transfer reactions indispensable for de novo purine and thymidylate biosynthesis. **High-dose methotrexate** at doses exceeding 1 g/m2 competitively inhibits **dihydrofolate reductase** DHFR, causing acute depletion of intracellular reduced folates. Safe administration strictly requires intensive intravenous sodium bicarbonate hydration maintaining urinary pH at or above 7.0 to prevent tubular precipitation of methotrexate and its insoluble metabolite 7-hydroxymethotrexate.
steps.say: Folate analogues block single-carbon transfer reactions indispensable for de novo purine and thymidylate biosynthesis. High-dose methotrexate at doses exceeding 1 g/m2 competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase DHFR, causing acute depletion of reduced folates. Safe administration strictly requires intensive intravenous hydration maintaining urinary pH at 7.0 or above to prevent renal tubular precipitation.

steps.tx: Systemic toxicity from methotrexate is averted by pharmacological bypass of the blocked enzymatic step. **Leucovorin calcium** folinic acid serves as the standard **pharmacological rescue** agent following high-dose methotrexate infusions. Administered every 6 hours starting 24 to 36 hours post-infusion, leucovorin provides reduced tetrahydrofolate directly to normal host tissues without requiring DHFR, continuing until serum methotrexate levels fall safely below 0.05 to 0.1 micromolar.
steps.say: Systemic toxicity from methotrexate is averted by pharmacological bypass of the blocked enzymatic step. Leucovorin calcium folinic acid serves as the standard pharmacological rescue agent following high-dose methotrexate infusions. Administered every 6 hours starting 24 to 36 hours post-infusion, leucovorin provides reduced folates directly to normal host tissues, bypassing DHFR.

left.title: Leucovorin Rescue Mechanism
points: Rescues bone marrow and gastrointestinal mucosa
Dosed according to serum methotrexate clearance nomogram

right.title: Folic Acid vs Leucovorin
points: Folic acid requires DHFR reduction (inactive during MTX)
Leucovorin does not require DHFR activation
Delayed leucovorin >42h causes irreversible mucosal necrosis
Competitive entry via reduced folate carrier RFC

steps.tx: Severe delayed methotrexate elimination in the setting of acute oliguric renal failure represents an oncologic emergency. **Glucarpidase** recombinant carboxypeptidase G2 functions as an enzymatic **antidote** for delayed clearance. Administered intravenously, glucarpidase rapidly cleaves extracellular methotrexate into inactive DAMPA within 15 minutes, lowering circulating methotrexate by over 95%. Importantly, leucovorin must be separated from glucarpidase by 2 hours because glucarpidase also hydrolyses leucovorin.
steps.say: Severe delayed methotrexate elimination in the setting of acute oliguric renal failure represents an oncologic emergency. Glucarpidase recombinant carboxypeptidase G2 functions as an enzymatic antidote for delayed clearance. Administered intravenously, glucarpidase rapidly cleaves extracellular methotrexate into inactive DAMPA within 15 minutes, lowering circulating drug levels by over 95%.

nodes.label: >95% Rapid Drop in Active MTX Levels

steps.tx: Fluoropyrimidine antineoplastic activity depends on differential intracellular metabolism and enzyme inhibition. **5-Fluorouracil** is converted into 5-FdUMP, which forms a stable covalent ternary complex with **thymidylate synthase** and reduced folates. In contrast to methotrexate rescue, the administration of exogenous leucovorin dramatically enhances 5-FU cytotoxicity by stabilising this inhibitory ternary complex, significantly increasing response rates in colorectal and gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas.

rows: Restores folate pool, prevents mucosal death
Stabilises TS-FdUMP ternary complex, boosts kill

steps.tx: Inherited pharmacogenetic defects in fluoropyrimidine catabolism precipitate catastrophic systemic toxicities. **Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase** DPD, encoded by the DPYD gene, catabolizes over 80% of administered 5-FU. Inherited **DPYD mutations**, particularly the splice variant DPYD*2A, cause complete or partial DPD deficiency, exposing patients to lethal neutropenic sepsis, enteritis, and neurotoxicity upon standard dosing. Pre-treatment DPYD genotyping directs vital upfront dose reductions.

Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase DPD, encoded by DPYD, catabolizes over 80% of administered 5-FU. Inherited DPYD mutations, particularly DPYD*2A, cause severe enzyme deficiency, exposing patients to lethal neutropenic sepsis, enteritis, and neurotoxicity.

left.title: Normal DPYD Function
points: Over 80% of 5-FU rapidly degraded in liver

right.title: DPYD Variant Alleles (e.g., *2A)
points: Mandates 50% dose cut or drug avoidance

steps.tx: Accidental fluoropyrimidine overdose or life-threatening early-onset toxicity is treatable with an approved oral antidote. **Uridine triacetate** acts as an effective competitive **toxicity rescue** agent against lethal 5-fluorouracil or capecitabine toxicities. Administered orally within 96 hours of drug exposure, uridine triacetate floods host cells with uridine triphosphate, competitively outcompeting toxic fluorouridine triphosphate for incorporation into RNA and rescuing mucosal and haematopoietic tissues.

Uridine triacetate acts as an effective competitive rescue agent against lethal 5-fluorouracil or capecitabine toxicities. Administered orally within 96 hours of exposure, it floods host cells with uridine, competitively blocking toxic RNA incorporation.

steps.tx: Novel multitargeted antifolates inhibit multiple distinct enzymes across the folate metabolic network. **Pemetrexed** is a pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that inhibits thymidylate synthase, DHFR, and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase. Approved for non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer and malignant pleural mesothelioma, clinical administration mandates prophylactic **folic acid** and vitamin B12 supplementation starting 1 week prior to therapy to suppress severe life-threatening haematologic and gastrointestinal toxicities.

steps.tx: Thiopurine antimetabolites are pro-drugs requiring intricate enzymatic activation and catabolism. **6-Mercaptopurine** 6-MP and **azathioprine** are converted to cytotoxic thioguanine nucleotides that incorporate into replicating DNA. Co-administration of the xanthine oxidase inhibitor **allopurinol** blocks the primary catabolic pathway into 6-thiouric acid, increasing circulating active metabolites four- to five-fold and provoking fatal bone marrow suppression unless thiopurine doses are pre-emptively reduced by 75%.
